messages:
tom.ops: FYI — during the partial eu-west GPU blip this morning we hit sustained queue depth spikes on the failover path. Need to update the runbook for queue sizing + operator scripts.

jess.sre: Ack. Saw the same. GPU util jumped ~92% and the queued inference requests piled up for ~6m.

oncall-bot: Incident detected: region-eu-west degraded (GPU utilization anomaly). Alerted at 2026-03-17T09:12Z.

akshay: Can someone paste the metric slices? I want seq_len and model type breakdown.

leo.eng: quick dump: model=redwood-4x, p50_latency=220ms -> p95=1.1s, queue_depth_peak=540, avg_seq_len=320. Most queued traffic was chat routing after primary capacity throttled.

maria.ops: Important note — the existing runbook assumes failover queue max_size=200. That proved too low when primary region slowed but didn't fully fail, because we were still accepting routed traffic.

jess.sre: Proposal: change default failover queue sizing logic to be dynamic: base = max(200, 0.5 * observed_inflight_primary) with max cap at 2000. Also add a short-circuit that drops non-critical lower-priority requests when queue > 1200.

amy.product: +1 to priority-based dropping. We should also list which routes are safe to deprioritize (background embeddings, batch rerank).

akshay: We should be careful about cost — increasing queue sizes can spike GPU memory pressure and increase eviction thrash. Add an autoscale hint instead of unbounded queue growth.

leo.eng: Agreed. Implementation idea: operator script will compute target_queue = clamp( max(200, inflight_primary*0.45), 200, 1500 ) and push to failover daemon via `rictl failover-config set --queue-size N`.

jess.sre: I'll draft the CLI snippet for runbook.

jess.sre: ```
# operator manual step
PRIMARY_INFLIGHT=$(rictl metrics get inflight --region eu-west)
TARGET=$(( PRIMARY_INFLIGHT * 45 / 100 ))
TARGET=$(python -c "print(min(max(200, int($TARGET)),1500))")
rictl failover-config set --queue-size $TARGET --reason "post-incident tuning"
```

maria.ops: Add to runbook: when adjusting queue_size, check `gpu_mem_free` and `eviction_rate`. If eviction_rate > 0.05/s, revert to previous size and trigger scaling instead.

akshay: Also add a preflight check that compares predicted latency: run synthetic probe to the failover path for p95 estimate before flipping traffic.

tom.ops: What about operator scripts that currently live in eng/tools? We should move a trimmed emergency copy into runbook repo under `playbooks/failover/` so oncall can run without git access to main repo.

leo.eng: I'll push a small script to runbook repo: `scripts/failover-queue-adjust.sh` with minimal dependencies. It will accept `--dry-run` and `--apply`.

amy.product: Please include a short blurb for customer-facing comms: we need a consistent phrasing: "We routed to a neighboring region; some lower-priority requests were delayed." Keep it non-technical.

jess.sre: Action items (I'll own):
- Update runbook step: dynamic queue sizing + thresholds (PR -> runbook repo)
- Add operator script copy to runbook repo (leo to implement)
- Add preflight synthetic latency probe and a decision gate (akshay)
- Add eviction-rate guard and revert logic (maria)
- Enumerate low-priority routes safe for dropping (amy/product)
- Add post-incident telemetry dashboard with queue_size, eviction_rate, synthetic p95 (jess)

maria.ops: Timeline? I can triage and get the runbook change live in 48 hours for a hotfix page, then we can refine infra code later.

leo.eng: I can have the script PR ready in 24 hours, ping me for review.

akshay: I'll mock up the probe in the next 36 hours and wire it to the decision gate.

tom.ops: Cool. Also we should schedule a 30m dry-run this week to simulate a partial region slowdown and exercise the new script — prefer Wed 09:00 PT.

amy.product: I'll prepare the comms template and a short FAQ item for customers who ask about "delays during region failover".

jess.sre: One more addendum to runbook: explicit rollback steps if failover daemon fails to apply new queue_size (example commands + who to call).

oncall-bot: Action items created: #INC-3142 (runbook update), #INC-3143 (script copy), #INC-3144 (probe), #INC-3145 (dashboard), assigned to owners.

tom.ops: Thanks everyone. Let's reconvene after the PRs land. If anyone hits a blocker, DM me. :thumbsup:
